title: How to use Notion Web Clipper on Mac: steps for Safari and Chrome, 2026
metaTitle: How to Use Notion Web Clipper on Mac (Safari and Chrome)
description: How to use Notion Web Clipper on Mac: install it in Chrome or Safari, log in, pick a database, and save any web page to Notion.
targetKeyword: how to use notion web clipper on mac
intro: On a Mac, Notion Web Clipper is a browser extension, so you install it in Chrome or Safari and log into Notion in that browser. Then click the Notion button beside the address bar, pick a workspace and a page or database, click Save page, and choose Open in Notion.
tldr: Notion Web Clipper is a browser extension, so on a Mac you use it in Chrome or Safari.
Chrome installs from the Chrome Web Store. Safari installs from notion.com/web-clipper, since the Safari clipper is no longer in the App Store.
Log into Notion in the same browser, then click the Notion button to save the page you are viewing.
Pick a workspace and a page or database, click Save page or press Enter, then choose Open in Notion.
Notion lists no clipper keyboard shortcut. Some guides cite ⌘⇧K, but that is unverified.

blocks.text: Notion Web Clipper is a small browser extension. It saves a web page into Notion so you can read it, tag it, and find it later. On a Mac, the clipper runs in Chrome or Safari, not inside the Notion desktop app. In Chrome, the Notion button sits to the right of the address bar once the extension is installed. The rest of this page covers installing the clipper, clipping a page, and fixing the common snags.
What you need before you install

items: A Mac with Chrome or Safari installed. Notion's help page lists only these two desktop browsers.
A Notion account with access to the workspace you want to clip into.
Permission to install browser extensions, and, for Safari, permission to open a downloaded app.
A web page open in the same browser, so there is something to save.

blocks.text: Log into Notion in the browser before you clip. The popup asks you to choose a workspace, so you need a live login there. If you use Chrome at work and Safari at home, install the clipper in both, and remember that each browser keeps its own login. Firefox, Edge, and Arc are not on Notion's list either, so check Notion's help page before you try them.
Install the clipper in Chrome on Mac

Open the Chrome Web Store listing for Notion Web Clipper and add it to Chrome. The listing names Notion Labs, Inc. as the developer. At the time of research, it showed version 0.2.20, last updated October 13, 2026. Store pages can lag behind the latest release, so treat the version number as a rough check, not a guarantee.
Install the clipper in Safari on Mac

Safari takes an extra step. Notion's help page says the Safari Web Clipper is no longer in the Apple App Store. You install it from notion.com/web-clipper instead. Open the downloaded disk image, move the app to Applications, and launch it. Then turn on the extension in Safari's Extensions settings. Notion's wording says only Safari's Extensions settings, so look under Settings in the Safari menu if you cannot find it at first.

blocks.text: How to clip a web page into Notion on Mac

Once the clipper is ready, the clip itself needs only a few choices. Open the page, then click the Notion button. The popup asks which workspace to use, then which page or database. A page suits a one-off note. A database suits anything you want to sort, filter, or review later.
Clip into a database and use the URL property

Notion's help page says that when you clip into a database, Notion adds a URL property automatically. That property stores the original web address, so you can always return to the source. Tags, other properties, comments, and edits come after the clip saves, inside Notion. That split is useful. Clip fast in the browser, then sort carefully in Notion.
Create a links database from the Add to menu

If you have no database for clips, open the Add to menu in the popup and choose + New links database. Name it something you will recognize later, such as Reading list or Research. Pick that database for your next clip. A links database works well for a set of sources you share with a team, because everyone sees the same URL column.
A worked example: saving an article to a reading list

Say you are reading a long article in Safari and want it in a shared Reading list database. Click the Notion button. Pick your team workspace. Pick the Reading list database, then click Save page. When the save finishes, choose Open in Notion, add a tag, and write a short line about why you saved it. The clip is then useful to someone else, not only to you.
Keyboard shortcuts on Mac: what Notion lists

Notion's keyboard shortcuts page covers Notion itself, not the clipper. It lists ⌘P or ⌘K to open search, which also jumps to recently viewed pages, and ⌘L to copy the current page's URL. It lists no save or clipper shortcut. In the clipper popup, Enter saves the page. Some third-party guides cite ⌘⇧K for the clipper, but Notion's own pages do not confirm it, so test it on your Mac before you rely on it.

items: ⌘P or ⌘K: open Notion search. It also jumps to recently viewed pages.
⌘L: copy the URL of the current Notion page. Handy for linking a clip from another page.
Enter: save the page from the clipper popup.
⌘⇧K: cited only by third-party guides. Unverified, so test it before you rely on it.

blocks.text: Plan limits that matter for shared workspaces

If your clips go into a shared team workspace, the plan matters. Notion's pricing page says the Free plan has a 5 MB per-file upload limit and 7-day page history. Solo Free users can add as many pages and blocks as they like. Multi-member Free workspaces get a limited number of blocks, and Notion does not state the number. Check the workspace plan before you clip a large batch.
Edge cases: when a clip looks wrong

Clips depend on the page. Notion's help page makes a warning about mobile clipping: formatting and some content may vary or be missing by site. The same caution fits the Mac clipper, so open each important clip and compare it with the original. Tables, code blocks, and images are the first places to check.
The old Safari App Store copy: clean it up first

Notion's help page says the Safari clipper is no longer in the App Store. If you installed the older App Store copy, remove it before you install the new one. Quit the app. Move it to the Trash, then empty the Trash. Uninstall any leftover extension in Safari's Extensions settings. Only then install the new version from notion.com/web-clipper. Leaving the old copy in place is the mistake to avoid.
When the Notion button does not show up

Start with three checks. Confirm the extension is installed and turned on. Confirm you are in Chrome or Safari, since Notion's help page lists no other desktop browsers. Confirm you are logged into Notion in that same browser. Notion's help page has no separate troubleshooting section for a missing button, so these checks come from its setup steps, not from a verified fix list.
When a clip saves but looks wrong

If a clip saves but looks off, open it in Notion and compare it with the original page. Clip again after the page has fully loaded. If clips fail in one browser but work in another, test the same page in the second browser to narrow it down. No official Notion article on silent save failures turned up at the time of research. If the problem keeps coming back, contact Notion support with your browser name, its version, and the page address.
Next steps after your first clip

Once your clips land in Notion, the next question is usually the desktop app. [How to install the Notion desktop app on Mac](/how-to/install-the-desktop-app-in-notion) walks through that setup in order. If Notion says your Mac is not supported, check [Notion system requirements on a Mac](/how-to/check-system-requirements-in-notion) first. Keep the clipper in the browser you use most, and add a second install only when you need it.

faq.question: Is there a Notion Web Clipper app for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, but it depends on the browser. The Safari version installs as a small app plus an extension from notion.com/web-clipper. Chrome uses an extension from the Chrome Web Store. You clip from inside the browser either way.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut for Notion Web Clipper on Mac?
faq.answer: Notion's keyboard shortcuts page lists no clipper shortcut. In the clipper popup, Enter saves the page. Some third-party guides cite ⌘⇧K, but Notion does not list it, so test it before you rely on it.

faq.question: Why does the Notion button not appear in Chrome?
faq.answer: Check that the extension is installed and turned on, and that you are in Chrome. Then confirm you are logged into Notion in the same browser. Notion's help page does not list a separate fix for a missing button.

faq.question: Can I clip into a database instead of a page?
faq.answer: Yes. Pick a database in the popup, or create one from the Add to menu with + New links database. Notion adds a URL property automatically to store the original web address.

faq.question: Does the clipper work in Firefox or Edge on Mac?
faq.answer: Notion's help page lists only Chrome and Safari as supported desktop browsers. Firefox, Edge, and Arc are not mentioned, so check Notion's help page before you rely on them.

faq.question: Do I need a paid Notion plan to use the clipper?
faq.answer: Notion's help page does not list plan limits for clipping. Notion's pricing page does list the Free plan's 5 MB per-file upload limit and 7-day page history, so check those if you clip into a shared workspace.

faq.question: Can I clip on my iPhone with the same tool?
faq.answer: Notion's help page covers mobile clipping separately. It works only for full web pages from a browser or photos from the photo roll, and it needs iOS 13.0 or later.

faq.question: Why did my clip lose some formatting?
faq.answer: Notion warns that formatting and some content can vary or go missing depending on the site. Open the saved clip, compare it with the original, and fix anything that moved.

appliesTo: Notion Web Clipper in Chrome or Safari on macOS

steps.name: Install the clipper in Chrome
steps.text: Open the Chrome Web Store listing for Notion Web Clipper. Notion Labs, Inc. is the listed developer. Click Add to Chrome and wait for the install to finish.
steps.tip: Check the developer name before you install, so you do not add a copy from another publisher.

steps.name: Install the clipper for Safari
steps.text: Download the Safari version from notion.com/web-clipper. Open the disk image and move the app to Applications. Launch the app once.
steps.tip: If an older App Store copy is installed, remove it first using the Trash steps further down the page.

steps.name: Turn on the Safari extension
steps.text: Open Safari's Extensions settings. Find Notion Web Clipper in the list and turn it on.
steps.tip: Notion's help page says only Safari's Extensions settings, so treat this menu path as a best guide.

steps.name: Log into Notion in the same browser
steps.text: Open notion.com in the browser where you installed the clipper and log in. The popup asks you to pick a workspace, so log in first.
steps.tip: Log in in each browser you clip from, since each one keeps its own session.

steps.name: Open the page you want to save
steps.text: Go to the article, product page, or document. Let it finish loading so the clip captures the full text.

steps.name: Open the Notion popup
steps.text: In Chrome, click the Notion button to the right of the address bar. In Safari, click the Notion icon the extension adds to your browser.

steps.name: Pick a workspace
steps.text: Choose the workspace where the clip should live from the popup. Check the name before you save, especially if you use more than one workspace.

steps.name: Choose a page or database
steps.text: Pick an existing page or database. To make a new links database, open the Add to menu and choose + New links database.

steps.name: Save the clip
steps.text: Click Save page, or press Enter. Wait for Notion to confirm the save before you close the popup.
steps.tip: Clips into a database add a URL property that stores the original address.

steps.name: Open the clip in Notion
steps.text: When the save finishes, choose Open in Notion. Add tags, properties, comments, or edits there.
steps.tip: The clipper only saves the page. Sorting and labeling happen inside Notion.

steps.name: Check the clip against the original
steps.text: Compare the saved clip with the original page. Look for missing images, broken layout, or missing text, then clip again if something important is gone.

shortcuts.action: Open Notion search (inside Notion, not the clipper)
Copy the URL of the current Notion page
Save the page from the clipper popup

troubleshooting.problem: No Notion button appears after installing
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the extension is installed and turned on. In Safari, turn it on in Extensions settings. Then confirm you are using Chrome or Safari, the two browsers Notion's help page lists.

troubleshooting.problem: The popup shows no workspace to choose
troubleshooting.fix: Log into Notion in the same browser, then click the Notion button again. The popup needs a login to offer a workspace.

troubleshooting.problem: Safari clipper behaves oddly after an earlier install
troubleshooting.fix: Remove any older App Store copy first. Quit the app, move it to the Trash, empty the Trash, and uninstall any leftover extension in Safari's Extensions settings. Then install from notion.com/web-clipper.

troubleshooting.problem: A saved clip has missing text or odd formatting
troubleshooting.fix: Compare it with the original page and fix the layout in Notion. Notion warns that clipping can vary by site, so some content may need manual repair.

troubleshooting.problem: A database clip has no link to the source
troubleshooting.fix: Clips into a database add a URL property automatically. Open the database and check the URL column before you assume the clip failed.
